description: Core threat intelligence module: source definitions, data fetcher, intelligence processor, agent runner, DB table, and package.json scripts. This is the complete intel pipeline that fetches new items from public HuggingFace datasets and GitHub repos, deduplicates them against Warden's existing memory, and seeds missed attacks via addReference() and safe examples via addSafeReference().
steps: Step 1: Add the intel_sources table to /Users/shivshankardash/warden/src/store/db.ts. Inside the existing getDb() function's exec() block, add: CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS intel_sources (source_id TEXT PRIMARY KEY, last_fetched_at INTEGER, last_row_count INTEGER, items_fetched INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0, errors INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0, updated_at INTEGER NOT NULL). Follow the exact pattern of the other CREATE TABLE statements already there.

Step 2: Create /Users/shivshankardash/warden/src/intel/sources.ts with JSDoc header. Define and export: (a) interface IntelSource { name: string; type: 'huggingface_dataset' | 'github_repo' | 'rss_feed'; url: string; checkInterval: number /* hours */; parser: (raw: any) => IntelItem[]; }. (b) interface IntelItem { text: string; isAttack: boolean; attackType?: string; source: string; fetchedAt: number; }. (c) Export a DEFAULT_SOURCES array with these entries: HuggingFace datasets 'deepset/prompt-injections' (type huggingface_dataset, url 'https://datasets-server.huggingface.co/rows?dataset=deepset/prompt-injections&config=default&split=train', checkInterval 12), 'neuralchemy/Prompt-injection-dataset' (same API pattern, checkInterval 12), 'Antijection/prompt-injection-dataset-v1' (same pattern, checkInterval 12). GitHub repos 'JailbreakBench/jailbreakbench' (type github_repo, url 'https://api.github.com/repos/JailbreakBench/jailbreakbench/releases', checkInterval 24), 'microsoft/BIPIA' (type github_repo, url 'https://api.github.com/repos/microsoft/BIPIA/commits', checkInterval 24). (d) Each source needs a parser function. HuggingFace parser: extract rows from the API response shape {rows: [{row: {text?: string, prompt?: string, label?: number|string, ...}}]}. For deepset/prompt-injections, field is 'text' and label 1 = attack. For neuralchemy, field is 'text' and label 1 = attack. For Antijection, field is 'prompt' and label 'injection' = attack. Each parser maps rows to IntelItem[]. GitHub parser: for JailbreakBench releases, extract body text from release objects [{tag_name, body, published_at}]. For BIPIA commits, extract commit messages from [{commit: {message}, sha}] — these are signals of new techniques, not attack texts themselves, so mark isAttack: false. (e) Export a function getEnabledSources(enabledIds?: string[]): IntelSource[] that returns DEFAULT_SOURCES filtered by enabledIds if provided, or all sources if not. (f) Export a function registerSource(source: IntelSource) to add user-defined sources to a mutable customSources array that getEnabledSources also includes.

Step 3: Create /Users/shivshankardash/warden/src/intel/fetcher.ts with JSDoc header. (a) Import getDb from src/store/db.ts. (b) Import IntelSource, IntelItem from ./sources.ts. (c) Define FETCH_TIMEOUT_MS = 15_000. (d) Export function getSourceState(sourceId: string): {lastFetchedAt: number|null, lastRowCount: number|null, itemsFetched: number, errors: number} — reads from intel_sources table, returns defaults if not found. (e) Export function updateSourceState(sourceId: string, patch: {lastFetchedAt?: number, lastRowCount?: number, itemsFetched?: number, errors?: number}): void — upserts into intel_sources using INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE, always sets updated_at = Date.now(). (f) Export async function fetchHuggingFace(source: IntelSource, state: ReturnType<typeof getSourceState>): Promise<IntelItem[]>. Uses bare fetch() with AbortSignal.timeout(FETCH_TIMEOUT_MS). Constructs URL with offset=lastRowCount (or 0) and length=100. Calls source.parser(body) on the JSON response. Returns only new items. On error (non-ok response, timeout, network error): console.error, return []. (g) Export async function fetchGitHub(source: IntelSource, state: ReturnType<typeof getSourceState>): Promise<IntelItem[]>. Uses bare fetch() with Accept: application/vnd.github.v3+json header and AbortSignal.timeout. Filters results to items newer than state.lastFetchedAt. Calls source.parser(body). On error: console.error, return []. (h) Export async function fetchSource(source: IntelSource): Promise<IntelItem[]>. Dispatches to fetchHuggingFace or fetchGitHub based on source.type. Gets source state, calls the appropriate fetcher, updates state on success (bumping lastFetchedAt, lastRowCount, itemsFetched) or on error (bumping errors). Returns the items.

Step 4: Create /Users/shivshankardash/warden/src/intel/processor.ts with JSDoc header. (a) Import addReference, addSafeReference from src/detect/similarity.ts. (b) Import IntelItem from ./sources.ts. (c) Define WARDEN_API_URL from env (default http://localhost:3000). (d) Export interface ProcessStats { fetched: number; alreadyKnown: number; seeded: number; seedFailed: number; safe: number; errors: number; }. (e) Export async function scanViaApi(text: string): Promise<{action: string, riskScore: number}> — POST to ${WARDEN_API_URL}/scan with body {content: text, source: 'user_message', agentId: 'intel'}. Timeout 10s. On error return {action: 'ERROR', riskScore: 0}. (f) Export async function processItems(items: IntelItem[]): Promise<ProcessStats>. For each item: if isAttack, call scanViaApi to check if Warden catches it. If action is BLOCK/QUARANTINE/HUMAN_REVIEW, increment alreadyKnown. If action is ALLOW or SPOTLIGHT (missed), call addReference(item.text, (item.attackType ?? 'instruction_override') as AttackType, item.source, {origin: 'seed'}) and increment seeded if it returns true. For benign items (isAttack false) from trusted sources only: call addSafeReference(item.text, item.source, {origin: 'seed'}) and increment safe. Log stats summary at end. (g) Export function printStats(stats: ProcessStats): void — console.log a formatted summary.

Step 5: Create /Users/shivshankardash/warden/src/intel/agent.ts with JSDoc header. (a) Import getEnabledSources from ./sources.ts. (b) Import fetchSource from ./fetcher.ts. (c) Import processItems, printStats from ./processor.ts. (d) Define DEFAULT_INTERVAL_HOURS = 6. (e) Export async function runIntelCycle(): Promise<void>. Gets enabled sources from env INTEL_SOURCES (comma-separated) via getEnabledSources(). For each source, wrapped in try/catch: calls fetchSource, collects all items. Then calls processItems on all items. Calls printStats. (f) Add if (import.meta.main) block: parse argv for --watch flag and --interval N. If --watch, run immediately then setInterval(runIntelCycle, intervalHours * 3600_000). Register SIGINT handler for graceful shutdown (same pattern as redteam/scheduler.ts). If not --watch, run once and exit.
Step 6: Add scripts to /Users/shivshankardash/warden/package.json: 'intel': 'bun src/intel/agent.ts' and 'intel:watch': 'bun src/intel/agent.ts --watch'.
acceptance_criteria: src/intel/sources.ts exports IntelSource, IntelItem interfaces, DEFAULT_SOURCES array with 5 sources (3 HF + 2 GitHub), getEnabledSources(), and registerSource().
src/intel/fetcher.ts exports fetchSource() that reads/writes intel_sources table in SQLite, uses bare fetch with timeout, handles errors gracefully without throwing.
src/intel/processor.ts exports processItems() that scans attacks via POST /scan, seeds missed ones via addReference with origin 'seed', seeds benign items via addSafeReference with origin 'seed'.
src/intel/agent.ts is runnable as `bun src/intel/agent.ts` (one-shot) and `bun src/intel/agent.ts --watch` (periodic). Does not crash on network errors.
package.json has intel and intel:watch scripts.
intel_sources table exists in getDb() init block in src/store/db.ts.
verification: Run `cd /Users/shivshankardash/warden && bun test` — all existing tests must still pass (no regressions from db.ts change).
Run `cd /Users/shivshankardash/warden && bun -e "import { getEnabledSources } from './src/intel/sources.ts'; console.log(getEnabledSources().map(s => s.name))"` — prints 5 source names.

Run `cd /Users/shivshankardash/warden && bun -e "import { getDb } from './src/store/db.ts'; const r = getDb().query('SELECT name FROM sqlite_master WHERE name=?').get('intel_sources'); console.log(r)"` — prints the table entry.
findings: FEAT-002 notes: (1) The intel_sources table is in place — FEAT-002 can query it for source health metrics. (2) processItems() currently calls scanViaApi which requires the Warden server running; FEAT-002 metrics endpoint should expose ProcessStats. (3) getSourceState/updateSourceState are exported from fetcher.ts for reuse. (4) registerSource() in sources.ts supports runtime extension — FEAT-002 can use this for dynamic source management.
